answer: Each participant’s challenge is derived from a committed identity and a future drand quicknet pulse, whose threshold-BLS output is unpredictable before release and publicly verifiable afterward. A quartz sample, prism rotation, or sparrow-pattern task can be prepared only once the pulse fixes its parameters, so precomputed answers and offline farming lose their advantage. Commit–reveal binds submissions to that challenge; enrollment limits and per-identity costs—not randomness alone—make spawning sybils uneconomic.
